summary:
FireWatch is an interactive data visualization tool that explores and compares historical active-fire detections across California using NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite observations.

The project brings together data from MODIS Terra, MODIS Aqua, and VIIRS Suomi-NPP, preserving their sensor information while organizing detections into a shared 1 km spatial grid and daily time framework.

Through an interactive dashboard, users can explore fire activity over time, visualize detection locations, examine confidence and Fire Radiative Power (FRP), and investigate where MODIS and VIIRS detections overlap or differ.

FireWatch focuses on making cross-sensor comparison easier by providing a common analytical framework for exploring how different satellite instruments observe fire activity. It serves as a starting point for further work in satellite data harmonization.
details:
FireWatch is an interactive dashboard designed to explore and compare active-fire detections from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite instruments across California.

How it works

The project combines historical observations from MODIS Terra, MODIS Aqua, and VIIRS Suomi-NPP, obtained through NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS).

To prepare the datasets for comparison, observations were filtered to California, and confidence values were standardized into common low, nominal, and high categories. Coordinates were transformed into California Albers (EPSG:3310) and assigned to a shared 1 km grid. Observations were then aggregated by date, grid cell, and sensor, allowing comparisons of detection counts, mean and maximum Fire Radiative Power (FRP), and mean brightness.

The dashboard allows users to filter by date and sensor and explore::

- Daily fire-detection activity charts.

- A calendar heatmap showing changes in activity over time.

- A map displaying sampled active-fire detection locations.

- Confidence-level distributions for each sensor.

- FRP summaries to explore the characteristics of detected hotspots.

- A spatial overlap comparison showing where both sensors recorded detections in the same grid cell on the same day.

Benefits and intended impact

MODIS and VIIRS have different spatial resolutions and detection characteristics. Bringing their observations into a shared analytical framework makes it easier to explore where their detections agree and differ. It provides a starting point for researchers and environmental monitoring teams to explore satellite observations and further investigate data harmonization

Tools and technologies

The project was developed using Python, Pandas, PyArrow, PyProj, Plotly, and Streamlit. Development was carried out using Visual Studio Code. NASA FIRMS supplied the satellite observation data. The final web application uses preprocessed Parquet datasets for efficient analysis and interactive visualization.

Creative approach and considerations

Rather than simply displaying detections on a map, FireWatch combines spatial and temporal analysis in one interactive environment.

California Albers was chosen because it provides projected coordinates in metres, making it possible to create consistent 1 km grid intervals. Latitude and longitude are measured in degrees, which do not represent consistent ground distances.

The analysis accounts for differences in sensor resolution, confidence reporting, acquisition times, and observation coverage. The shared grid does not mean the original sensor pixels are identical, and detections in the same cell on the same day do not necessarily represent the same individual fire

Future development

Future improvements could include expanding the analysis beyond California, testing different spatial and temporal matching methods, and introducing near-real-time mapping. This would help make FireWatch more useful for exploring ongoing fire activity as well as historical patterns.
